characterList.description: A middle-aged man with graying blonde hair, wearing a black suit, white shirt, and a black tie with gold crests. He is the interviewee and a candidate for the presidency of the United States.
characterList.name: Virgil Goode

content_metadata.description: An interview with Virgil Goode, a presidential candidate, discussing his policy stances and candidacy.

qAndA.answer: Goode has graying blonde hair, wears a black suit, white shirt, and a black tie with gold crests.
qAndA.question: What specific details about Goode's appearance help you identify him?

qAndA.answer: Goode argues that legal immigration is negatively impacting the job market and that it's time to prioritize American citizens. He states that 1.2 million people come into the country on green cards each year and that a large portion of those people take jobs that 'should go to US citizens.'
qAndA.question: What is Goode's main argument against legal immigration?

qAndA.answer: Goode argues against automatic birthright citizenship for children born to illegal aliens in the US, claiming they strain social welfare programs. This connects to his overall stance on stricter immigration control and prioritizing resources for American citizens.
qAndA.question: How does Goode's view on automatic birthright citizenship connect to his stance on illegal immigration?

qAndA.answer: The interview maintains a mostly neutral and pensive tone, reflecting Goode's serious and thoughtful approach to policy issues. This mood reinforces his message of focusing on practical solutions and responsible governance.
qAndA.question: What is the general mood of the interview, and how does it contribute to Goode's message?

qAndA.answer: By consistently highlighting US sovereignty, Goode seeks to appeal to voters concerned about the potential erosion of national independence. This theme resonates with his stance against globalism and international agreements that could potentially undermine US autonomy.
qAndA.question: What is the significance of Goode's repeated emphasis on US sovereignty?

activities.description: Goode introduces himself and his candidacy.
Goode discusses his plans if elected, including balancing the budget, reducing legal immigration, imposing term limits, and focusing on the American citizen.
Goode criticizes the fundraising practices of President Obama and Mitt Romney.
Goode invites viewers to donate to his campaign and visit his website.
Goode expresses his opposition to Agenda 21 and globalism.
Goode discusses his stance on the National Defense Authorization Act and his opposition to certain provisions.
Goode shares his views on illegal immigration, arguing for stricter measures and a focus on American citizens.
Goode reiterates his opposition to globalism and a North American Union, emphasizing the importance of US sovereignty.
Goode expresses his stance against the North American Union and the New World Order, emphasizing the sovereignty of the United States.
Goode answers a question about his opinion on the TSA 'groping people' and closes the interview.

characterInteraction.description: Goode interacts with an unseen interviewer, responding to questions and explaining his positions.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Goode consistently emphasizes the importance of US sovereignty and expresses opposition to any form of global governance.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Slightly Happy and Excited mood as Goode introduces his candidacy. Transitions to Pensive as he begins discussing his policy stances.
Mood shifts to slightly Angry as Goode addresses the TSA practices. Returns to Neutral as he closes the interview.

narrativeProgression.description: The video primarily presents a collection of Goode's views and policy stances rather than a narrative story.

The section discussing donations and Goode's website could be shortened or moved to a separate call to action.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: My name is Virgil Goode.
All right.
A candidate of the Constitution Party for the presidency of the United States.
We're currently on the ballot at 17 states and we're getting petitions to secure ballot access
and hopefully between 40 and 50 states.
So what will you plan to do when becoming president?
We need to do four things right away.
One, have a balanced budget.
The debt and deficit are staggering for this country.
Under President Obama, the debt has increased by $5 trillion.
We will end up like Greece or a third world country if the borrowing does not stop.
It would be my plan to submit a balanced budget sooner, not later as proposed by the Democrats and Republicans.
Second, for the jobs and economy, we need to take the step of reducing legal immigration.
Right now, 1.2 million persons come into this country on green cards every year.
Two-thirds to three-fourths of that 1.2 million take jobs that should go to U.S. citizens.
It's time to place the American citizen first.
When I'm elected, we are going to have an administration where citizenship means something.
Jobs in America for American citizens.
Third, I believe in term limits.
If I'm elected, I will serve only one term as president.
We also need term limits on the U.S. Senate and the U.S. House of Representatives.
Fourth and last, we need someone in the office of president that is a grassroots person
that isn't focused on raising big money from Wall Street or from Hollywood.
President Obama just held a big fundraiser hosted by George Clooney that raised tens of millions of dollars.
On the Republican side, you have candidate Mitt Romney that is appealing to many of the Wall Street friends of his.
And that's where his big money is coming from.
My donations are limited to individuals at a sum of $2 to $200.
If you would like to make a contribution to virtual good for president between $2 and $200, we would certainly appreciate it.
You can visit my website, goodforpresentat20toyup.com.
What is your view on agenda 21?
I'm opposed to agenda 21.
This is really a scheme, if you will, that the UN and globalists want to impose more regulations on the United States citizens and the businesses and the farms in this country.
I'm opposed to it.
What will you do in regards to the National Defense Authorization Act for fiscal year 2012 and 2013?
Parts of that act, in my view, do not comport with the United States Constitution.
I would veto the measure and gotten the unconstitutional provisions correct.
What is your view on illegal immigration?
The illegal immigration must be totally stopped.
We are a magnet to attract persons from other countries that want to come to this country and get benefits.
For example, the children of illegal aliens born in the United States get automatic birthright citizenship.
They then get Medicaid, they get food stamps, they get public assistance.

We need to change automatic birthright citizenship so that the children of illegal immediately don't step into the federal trough and get the money that hard earn tax pay as a pay to the federal treasury.
What is your view on globalism, a world government?
The United States should always place its Constitution first.
We should not be subject to a globalism philosophy.
I believe in the sovereignty of the United States and running on the Constitution Party ticket, which I'm climbing up Pennsylvania, we believe that the Constitution is the supreme document.
Not the UN Charter or any globalist treaty or agreement.
So that means that you're against the plan for North American Union?
Absolutely. In the US H such as representatives, I was the chief sponsor of legislation aimed at blocking the North American Union.
So have you heard of the so-called bilgerberg group that meets every four years in North America?
I don't know where they meet. I have heard of them.
Again, though, I believe in the sovereignty of the United States and not a march towards a globalism where the United States has its sovereignty subsumed into some international group or entity.
It's time to place, as I said at the beginning, the United States is first, I'm for citizenship.
First, and I believe citizenship matters and we need to focus on our country and not be spending so much on falling at it.
So, you will literally, I mean, as President, you would literally go against the so-called plan for a new world order.
Absolutely. The new world order would place US citizens under the jurisdiction of a world court.
It would place the persons in the army and the navy and the Marines in all our branches of service under that jurisdiction ultimately.
And I believe, as I said before, in the sovereignty of the United States first, I'm not for the new world order.
All right. I've got a very good last question. It just came to mind. What do you think about the TSA group and people?
Well, I think that needs to be reshaped and redone. I think that's uncalled for.
I want us to be safe, but there are ways that that can be handled outside of the broken persons and that a lot of other countries don't be there.
All right. This is the interview with Brian D. Hill, reporter for USWGO, and we are Change North Carolina.
Interview in your name?
Virtual Goode from Virginia. And we're working to get signatures in North Carolina, Virginia and Hollywood, the country.
And I would appreciate you voting in 2012 for President.
Thank you. It was a pleasure doing the interview.
All right. Thank you.

Questions were asked to Presidential Candidate Virgil Goode on his viewpoint 0n Globalism and the New World Order, the Bilderberg Group, and NDAA and he is dead set against it.

According to the interview he is a candidate trying to become the President of the United States for 2012 and wants to start blocking a lot of the terrible things heading for America which is a globalist controlled World Government, illegal immigration, and abortion.

Before the interview USWGO conducted an intelligence gathering operation to be able to brief to the public who this guy is and why he was at Blue Grass event at The Patrick County Music Association, May 26th 2012. First of all he was gathering petition signatures via a legal ballot petition document. It usually requires 10,000 signatures and the last 4 digits of the persons social security number and the person has to be registered to vote in order to sign this petition. With enough signatures on the petition for each state, each state will then add the candidate to the official voting ballot. Virgil Goode is apart of the Constitution party which is outside of the usual democrat and republican paradigm. He was nominated by the Constitution party to be a candidate for the President of the United States. He used to be a U.S. senator, then a U.S. Congressman. He was democrat and then Republican and then now he became a Constitutional party candidate. The fact he admits he is discovering about thew Bilderberg Group and Globalism existing is why he has quit the left right paradigm.

He is a very nice fellow, very humble, and is working like crazy to be able to become president to reverse a lot of the travesties that past presidents have formed and created.

He wishes to bring America back to being under a Constitution instead of a fiat dictatorship.
